Gwent is an old card game particularly popular among dwarves. It depicts a battle between two armies: the players are generals, and their cards represent their units. Each player uses their own deck, built around one of five factions: Monsters, Nilfgaardian Empire, Northern Realms, Scoia\'tael and Skellige. Each faction has unique cards that support different play styles. Neutral cards can be used by any faction. The goal is to win two rounds out of three by having greater total strength than your opponent.

At the start of the first round, each player draws ten cards from their deck. You may then replace up to two cards, drawing a new card for each one you replace. The replaced cards are shuffled back into your deck. Determine the starting player by flipping a coin.
Players take turns. On your turn, either play a card or pass. Once you pass, you cannot play any more cards for the rest of the round. Your opponent may continue playing cards until they also pass. A player with no cards left must pass.
The round ends when both players have passed. The player with the higher total score wins the round. If the scores are tied, both players win the round. At the end of each round, cards on the battlefield are moved to their owners\' discard piles. You keep your remaining hand for the next round—you do not draw new cards. The winner of the previous round takes the first turn. The goal of the game is to win two rounds.

There are five factions: Monsters, Nilfgaardian Empire, Northern Realms, Scoia\'tael and Skellige. Each faction has unique cards, leaders and a faction perk. Neutral cards can be used in any faction\'s deck.

The Monsters faction is led by Eredin Bréacc Glas, also known as Sparrowhawk, the King of the Wild Hunt. Its Iron Skin perk lets you keep one random unit on the battlefield at the end of each round.
Emhyr var Emreis, also known as \"The White Flame Dancing on the Barrows of his Enemies\", is the emperor of Nilfgaard. The Nilfgaardian faction\'s Treachery perk lets it win tied rounds.
The Northern Realms are led by Foltest, King of Temeria. Their faction perk lets you draw one card after winning a round.
The Scoia\'tael are nonhuman rebels fighting against oppression by the Northern Realms. They are led by Francesca Findabair, also known as Enid an Gleanna (Daisy of the Valleys). Their faction perk lets you choose who takes the first turn in the first round.
Skellige\'s faction perk places two random unit cards from your discard pile on the battlefield at the start of the third round.

Each faction offers a choice of leaders with different abilities, listed below.

Monsters: Eredin Bréacc Glas

The Treacherous:
Passive: Double the strength of all spy cards belonging to either player.

Bringer of Death:
Discard two cards, then draw one card of your choice from your deck.

Commander of the Red Riders:
Choose a weather card from your deck and play it immediately.

King of the Wild Hunt:
Double the strength of all your close combat units unless a Commander\'s Horn is already present in that row.

Destroyer of Worlds:
Return a card from your discard pile to your hand.

Nilfgaardian Empire: Emhyr var Emreis

The Relentless:
Draw a card from your opponent\'s discard pile.

The White Flame:
Cancel your opponent\'s leader ability.

Invader of the North:
Abilities that return a unit to the battlefield now return a randomly chosen unit. This affects both players.

Emperor of Nilfgaard:
Look at three random cards from your opponent\'s hand.

His Imperial Majesty:
Choose a Torrential Rain card from your deck and play it immediately.

Northern Realms: Foltest

The Steel-Forged:
Destroy all your opponent\'s siege units tied for the highest strength if the total strength of their siege units is at least 10.

Lord Commander of the North:
Remove all weather effects currently in play.

The Siegemaster:
Double the strength of all your siege units unless a Commander\'s Horn is already present in that row.

King of Temeria:
Choose an Impenetrable Fog card from your deck and play it immediately.

Son of Medell:
Destroy all your opponent\'s ranged combat units tied for the highest strength if the total strength of their ranged combat units is at least 10.

Scoia\'tael: Francesca Findabair

Daisy of the Valley:
Draw an extra card at the beginning of the battle.

Hope of the Aen Seidhe:
Move agile units to whichever permitted row gives them the greatest strength. Do not move units already in their optimal row.

Queen of Dol Blathanna:
Destroy all your opponent\'s close combat units tied for the highest strength if the total strength of their close combat units is at least 10.

The Beautiful:
Double the strength of all your ranged combat units unless a Commander\'s Horn is already present in that row.

Pureblood Elf:
Choose a Biting Frost card from your deck and play it immediately.

Skellige

Crach an Craite:
Shuffle all cards from both players\' discard piles back into their owners\' decks.

King Bran:
Units lose only half their strength in bad weather.

There are three main types of cards: leader cards, unit cards and special cards. Each deck contains one leader card with an ability that can be activated once per game.
A deck must also contain at least 22 unit cards, including any heroes. Heroes are immune to effects that increase or reduce strength. Players take turns playing their units. Each player has three combat rows: close combat, ranged combat and siege. Each unit card indicates which row it can be played in.
A deck may contain up to ten special cards, such as Decoy, Scorch, Commander\'s Horn, Mardroeme and weather cards. Weather cards are placed in a separate area of the board because they affect both players. Commander\'s Horn is placed in the combat row it affects.

Some unit cards have special abilities, described below.

Spy:
Play this card on your opponent\'s side of the battlefield, where it counts toward their total score, and draw two additional cards from your deck.

Tight Bond:
When placed next to a card with the same name, double the strength of both cards.

Muster:
When you play this card, find all cards with the same name in your deck and play them immediately.

Morale Boost:
Increase the strength of all other units in this row by one.

Medic:
Choose a unit card from your discard pile and play it immediately. Heroes and special cards cannot be chosen. Agile units must return to their previous combat row.

Commander\'s Horn:
Double the strength of all other units in this combat row.

Agile:
Play this card in either the close combat or ranged combat row. It cannot be moved after it has been played.

Scorch:
Destroy all units tied for the highest strength in the specified combat row on your opponent\'s side of the battlefield.

Clan Dimun Pirate:
Unlike other units with Scorch, playing this card destroys all cards tied for the highest strength on the entire battlefield, just like a Scorch special card.

Summon Avenger:
When this card is removed from the battlefield, summon a powerful replacement unit.

Mardroeme:
Transform all Berserkers in the same combat row into bears.

Berserker:
This unit transforms into a bear when Mardroeme is present in the same combat row. The transformation is permanent.

You can play a special card instead of a unit card on your turn. Their effects are described below.

Biting Frost:
Set the strength of all close combat units to one for both players.

Impenetrable Fog:
Set the strength of all ranged combat units to one for both players.

Torrential Rain:
Set the strength of all siege units to one for both players.

Skellige Storm:
Apply the effects of Impenetrable Fog and Torrential Rain to both players\' ranged combat and siege rows, just as if both weather cards had been played.

Clear Weather:
Remove all weather effects.

Decoy:
Swap this card with a unit card on your side of the battlefield, returning that unit to your hand.

Commander\'s Horn:
Double the strength of all units in the selected combat row.

Scorch:
Destroy all cards tied for the highest strength on the battlefield, then discard this card.

Mardroeme:
Transform all Berserkers in the selected combat row into bears.

Thanks for installing Dandelion\'s Calculator! Please note that this app is made to support you in playing Gwent using analog cards by calculating your points. This app does not allow you to play Gwent against AI or without analog cards!

So if you didn\'t do so yet: Print out a deck of Gwent cards (guidance here) and find an opponent who does the same (both of you need to install this app).

Your game board consists of three combat rows: Close combat, Ranged combat and Siege row (left to right). These rows contain unit cards. Each of them can be weakened by certain weather cards or boosted by a Commander\'s Horn.

Combat rows consist of the following parts:

1: Overall strength of all units placed in this row.

2: The current weather (can be changed by tapping).

3: The boost of a Commander\'s Horn (can be changed by tapping).

4: Number of units in this combat row (you can add or remove units by tapping).

Next to the game board there is a menu providing useful functions:

1: Overall strength of all units

2: Change faction

3: Reset board

4: Clear weather

5: Scorch strongest unit(s)

6: Coin-flip

7: Settings

More information on Gwent and its rules can be found in the settings. There you can repeat this introduction too!

But first: Have fun with analog Gwent! Please use the Google Play Store or GitHub to share improvement suggestions, bugs and other feedback with me!
